L2564@P60: Recursive Orthogonal Vector Projection Algorithm for Linear Spectral Unmixing
L2565@P60: Meiping Song, Information and Technology College, Dalian Maritime University, Dalian, China

L2570@P60: Engineering, University of Maryland, Baltimore County, Baltimore, USA
L2571@P60: Abstract : Orthogonal vector projection (OVP) is recently developed as a versatile technique which can used in various application in hyperspectral imaging such as subpixel detection, linear spectral unmixing and endmember finding. A great
L2572@P60: advantage of OVP is that only calculations of vector products are required with no need of matrix multiplications and inverse
L2573@P60: calculations. Furthermore, this paper develops a recursive version of OVP, to be called recursive OVP (ROVP) so that OVP can
L2574@P60: be performed vector by vector recursively without using previously processed vectors. As a result, the computational complexity
L2575@P60: of ROVP is much lower than other algorithms. Furthermore, the ROVP is much easier to be applied to hardware such as FPGA
L2576@P60: or GPU in the future.
L2577@P60: MULTILAYER STRUCTURED NMF FOR SPECTRAL UNMIXING OF HYPERSPECTRAL IMAGES
L2578@P60: Roozbeh Rajabi and Hassan Ghassemian, ECE Department, Tarbiat Modares University, Tehran, Iran
L2579@P60: Abstract : One of the challenges in hyperspectral data analysis is the presence of mixed pixels. Mixed pixels are the result
L2580@P60: of low spatial resolution of hyperspectral sensors. Spectral unmixing methods decompose a mixed pixel into a set of endmembers
L2581@P60: and abundance fractions. Due to nonnegativity constraint on abundance fraction values, NMF based methods are well suited to
L2582@P60: this problem. In this paper multilayer NMF has been used to improve the results of NMF methods for spectral unmixing of hyperspectral data under the linear mixing framework. Sparseness constraint on both spectral signatures and abundance fractions
L2583@P60: matrices are used in this paper. Evaluation of the proposed algorithm is done using synthetic and real datasets in terms of spectral
L2584@P60: angle and abundance angle distances. Results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms other previously proposed methods.
L2585@P60: ON THE USE OF RITZ VALUES FOR CALCULATING THE NUMBER OF ENDMEMBERS IN HYPERSPECTRAL IMAGES
L2586@P60: Raúl Guerra, Sebastián López, Gustavo M. Callico, Jose F. Lopez and Roberto Sarmiento,
L2587@P60: Institute for Applied Microelectronics (IUMA), University of Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, Spain
L2588@P60: Abstract : Signal subspace identification is a crucial step in many hyperspectral processing algorithms such as target
L2589@P60: detection, change detection, classification, and unmixing. This is due to the fact that a correct dimensionality reduction improves
L2590@P60: algorithm performances and reduces their complexity and data requirements.
L2591@P60: This paper introduces a new method for this task which is based on the Ritz values obtained in methods such as the
L2592@P60: restarted Arnoldi method or the Lanczos method for calculating the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a given matrix. In particular,
L2593@P60: it first calculates a high number of eigenvalues and eigenvectors, and a Ritz value per eigenvalue calculated and then, it estimates
L2594@P60: the dimension of the signal subspace according to the Ritz values obtained. The results obtained with the proposed method for
L2595@P60: synthetic and real hyperspectral images verify the performance of the introduced methodology to estimate the number of endmembers in different types of hyperspectral images. Moreover, these results are better than the ones obtained, for the same images,
L2596@P60: with the most popular algorithm for this task in the state of the art, i.e. the HySIME and the Virtual Dimensionality algorithms.

L2607@P61: Session thu-p-b : Feature extraction, band selection and dimension reduction
L2608@P61: Abstract : The linear mixing model (LMM) is a widely used methodology for the spectral unmixing (SU) of hyperspectral data. In this model, hyperspectral data is formed as a linear combination of spectral signatures corresponding to macroscopically pure materials (endmembers), weighted by their fractional abundances. Some of the drawbacks of the LMM are the presence
L2609@P61: of multiple mixtures and the spectral variability of the endmembers due to illumination and atmospheric effects. These issues
L2610@P61: appear as variations of the spectral conditions of the image along its spatial domain. However, these effects are not so severe locally and could be at least mitigated by working in smaller regions of the image. The proposed local SU works over a partition of
L2611@P61: the image, performing the spectral unmixing locally in each region of the partition. In this work, we first introduce the general
L2612@P61: local SU methodology, then we propose an implementation of the local SU based on a binary partition tree representation of the
L2613@P61: hyperspectral image and finally we give an experimental validation of the approach using real data.
